ov: A domesticated rodent first bred for meat in the Andes as early as 5000 BC, and now a popular pet. It isn’t found in the wild at all.

why.ac: Guinea pigs are crepuscular, most active at dawn and dusk.
why.et: Guinea pigs, called cuy, are still raised for meat in the Andes of South America.
why.p: Kept as pets worldwide, though first domesticated in the Andes for meat.

rg: Domestic worldwide. It comes from the Andean region of South America and has no wild population.
df: A plant-eater. Unlike rabbits, guinea pigs can’t make their own vitamin C, so they need it in their food.
notes: The existing fact (not a pig, nothing to do with Guinea) is confirmed: not native to Guinea, not closely related to pigs, and the origin of the name is unclear.
